properties.areaDesc: Canyon Ferry Area; Missouri Headwaters; Gallatin Valley
properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 13 at 2:01PM MDT until October 14 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Highly variable visibility as low as one quarter of a mile
in dense fog.

* WHERE...Canyon Ferry Area, Gallatin Valley, and Missouri
Headwaters.

* WHEN...From 9 PM this evening to noon MDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Below freezing temperatures tonight may lead
to a glaze of ice on surfaces, most notably on bridges and
overpasses.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

NWSheadline: DENSE FOG ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 9 PM THIS EVENING TO NOON MDT WEDNESDAY

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 13 at 8:53AM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by Thursday night. Widespread showers may
be heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of thunderstorms.
Landslides will also be possible along steep mountainous terrain.
Impacts could begin as early as Thursday and are expected to
persist through the weekend. While there is still uncertainty in
the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan now for wet
conditions that could persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Thursday night through Sunday

properties.areaDesc: Jefferson; Shelby
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 13 at 2:33PM CDT by NWS Birmingham AL
properties.description:
AQABMX

The Alabama Department of Environmental Management, ADEM, has issued
an Air Quality Alert for Jefferson and Shelby Counties for
Wednesday, October 14.

Under Code Orange conditions, ground level ozone concentrations are
expected to reach levels that are unhealthy for sensitive groups.
Children and people with asthma are individuals most at risk under
these expected conditions.

ADEM recommends the following actions during an air quality alert
for ozone:

Conserve electricity and set your air conditioner at a higher
temperature.

Limit driving and combine errands.

Use the bus or car pool to work.

Avoid use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment.

Refuel cars and trucks after 6 PM.

Limit engine idling.

Use household, workshop, and garden chemicals in ways that keep
evaporation to a minimum, or try to avoid them when poor air quality
is forecast.

If breathing becomes difficult, move indoors.

For more information on what to do on an air quality alert day,
visit the Environmental Protection Agency website at airnow.gov
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: CODE ORANGE AIR QUALITY ALERT HAS BEEN ISSUED FOR JEFFERSON AND SHELBY COUNTIES
